The high ceiling and the semi-arched brick back bar give a good sense of space, and the appropriate lighting that fills the space, speakers with great sound, and the comfort of comfortable chairs make it difficult to feel like standing up once you sit down.
It's an unfamiliar space, but the Jim Beam Blacks lined up behind pretty glasses give me a nice feeling that this place is continuing from Hell Cafe Spirits.
.
Even though it was the first day, the customer service was thorough and friendly (maybe because there were people I knew). They also pay a lot of attention to cleanliness. (In a way, it's natural, but before you sit down, you do a QR check-in and temperature check, and as soon as you sit down, they squeeze out hand sanitizer and provide wet tissues so you can wipe your hands every time you pick something up or go out.)
.
The welcome food was great as a side dish as it whetted the appetite and did not interfere with the drink. I thought it was a lot to eat alone, but I ate almost all of it ^^7
.
You guys are really good at drinks, so what can I say...
Nevertheless, the Godfather made with Stag Junior after a long time was really... as it was before, it was shockingly good. I don't really like Stag Junior because I keep comparing it to George T. Stag, but this Godfather is the best... It is diluted appropriately, so the aroma and taste of the host awakens, the strong body, which can be a bit burdensome, becomes moderately calm, and the amaretto melts in with a sense of unity, making it perfect. You could say that Godfather was originally like that, but achieving this level of perfection is easier said than done...
.
Even though I had high expectations for the new space, it was a satisfying time. It was even better because I was able to meet people I hadn't seen in a long time.

reviews.text:
Hidden beneath Apgujeong Rodeo, Don’t Tell Mama is a bar with a playful name—but a surprisingly warm and welcoming atmosphere. Despite the cheeky branding, it’s the kind of place you could comfortably visit even with your mom. The service is truly kind and attentive.
The bartenders are young, yet clearly seasoned. Their drinks reflect solid fundamentals rather than flashy trends. Some cocktails carry names that might be difficult to post in a public review—witty, slightly mischievous—but the flavors themselves are sincere and beautifully balanced. Layered aromas, thoughtful structure, and a clean finish show real craftsmanship.
English is spoken comfortably, and a bit of Japanese as well. It’s an easy spot to bring international friends.
Beneath the glamor of Apgujeong Rodeo, this underground bar quietly builds its reputation on skill and personality. You might stop in for one drink—but thanks to the bartender’s humor and charm, you’ll likely order another.

A space with a witty name, found in the basement of Apgujeong Rodeo.
The name of the business, Don Tell Mama, is a bit playful, but once you enter, the atmosphere is surprisingly warm and comfortable. The response is so gentle and attentive that it doesn't feel awkward at all even if you come with your mother.

It feels like the balance of ingredients, the layers of scent, and the neatness of the finish have been calculated.
English is spoken naturally, and Japanese is fluent. Feel free to visit with foreign friends.
Beneath the splendor of Apgujeong Rodeo, a space where skills were quietly built underground.
This is a place where you go for a quick drink and end up ordering another drink with the bartender telling a joke.
Although it is called “Don’t tell mom”,

Melody that fills Apgujeong’s night: Bourbon Street

In the heart of bustling Apgujeong, there are nights when you just want to block out the noise of the world and immerse yourself in the beauty of music and premium drinks.

Today, I would like to record my experience at Bourbon Street, a hidden gem in Sinsa-dong.

Melodious Canary: Performance by Eri Yazaki

The moment I opened the door and entered, deep, resonant music filled the air and captivated me.

Eri Yazaki's performance exceeded expectations.

Her clear and delicate voice, like a bird, put everyone in the bar into a breathtaking ecstasy.
As soon as the melody enveloped the entire space, I realized why I seek out bars with live music. For that moment when everything in the world feels unimportant and you are immersed solely in music.

Professionalism in every detail

What made this place truly special was the incredibly professional attitude of the bartenders. Beyond simply making drinks, their innate ability to read the atmosphere and provide service with genuine consideration stood out.

From the precise movements of the bartenders to the attentive and skillful service, it perfectly combines formal yet warm hospitality.
The excellence of this place goes without saying.

The beauty of alcohol and hope for the future

Cocktails were also great.

The perfect combination of ingredients enriched the lingering sound of the music.

In a rapidly changing neighborhood like Apgujeong, it was truly meaningful to discover a space that remains constant and serves as a ‘window of opportunity’ for talented artists and musicians.

I sincerely hope that this place will remain a haven for music lovers for a long time to come and become a landmark for artistic passion.

visiting point

Atmosphere: An upscale live music bar where you can focus entirely on the voices of the artists.

Located along Dosan-daero in Sinsa-dong, Gangnam-gu, it is one of the three largest private museums in Korea. It was founded by Horim Yoon Jang-seop. It was established in Daechi-dong in 1982, with the main building later relocated to Sillim-dong, and a Shinsa branch opened in Gangnam in 2009. It is an important museum that continuously exhibits Korea's high-class ancient art collection in the form of special exhibitions. The main building is operated in the form of a permanent exhibition, and the branch building is operated in the form of a special special exhibition. This time, there is a special exhibition focusing on Japanese paintings among the collections, so I saw the exhibition, and it runs until September 29th. It's a great opportunity to see Japanese ancient art that you don't normally see.

It's been a while since I visited again to see the Joseon Western Painting Exhibition. It was an opportunity to appreciate many cultural assets themed around Joseon gardens, from calligraphy and painting to ceramics from the Joseon Dynasty. In particular, I saw Donggwoldo again after a long time, and it was a bit disappointing because it was a replica. However, Jeongseon's beautiful paintings and elegant folding screens were rarely seen, but I got the chance to see them this time. It's well organized so you can look around leisurely.

I learned that Teacher Ahn Chang-ho believed that education and enlightenment were the path to independence during the Japanese colonial era when our people were losing their direction, so he established Dosan Academy in South Pyongan Province to teach young people, and later organized the Shinminhoe to try to foster the independent power of the nation. Also, after exiled to Shanghai, China, I learned that he became the center of the independence movement by acting as the first Prime Minister of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea, enacting the Provisional Charter and reorganizing the organization. I learned that he even founded Heungsadan in the United States to teach national spirit and moral leadership to youth, and I was really impressed by the fact that he even led the unity of overseas compatriots. From Teacher Ahn Chang-ho, I learned what a true leader is who sacrifices himself for his country.
What I want to say to you, teacher, is that I really, really appreciate you fighting so hard using ‘education’ and ‘character’ as your weapons instead of guns or violence. Because you believed that only by living righteously can the country stand upright, I think we today can proudly say that we are ‘citizens of the Republic of Korea.’ thank you. As I learned about Teacher Ahn Chang-ho's endless patience and human warmth, I came to realize the great meaning that true independence begins with independence in the heart.
From now on, I want to follow your example and live as a person who is not afraid of doing the right thing. I will fulfill my responsibilities even in small things, will not remain silent about injustice, and will not stop trying to grow myself. I promise to become the ‘people who stand upright on their own’ that Teacher Ahn Chang-ho dreamed of.

Dosan Park.

A park with a memorial hall and statue of independence activist Dosan Ahn Chang-ho.
It is said that his remains and those of his wife, Mrs. Lee Hye-ryeon, who were originally buried in Manguri, Gyeonggi-do, were moved here in 1973 and buried together, creating a park.
You will arrive after passing a street lined with luxury goods and brand stores.
In fact, when you walk through the park, you will see that the level of maintenance of the park is similar to that of old parks (since there are many well-built parks in recent years). For a park built for a great man who contributed to the country, I think the level of maintenance is not good enough (especially in Gangnam local government, which has a lot of money.) For this reason, I felt a little bitter.
Other than this, it is a place where you can get a glimpse of Dosan Ahn Chang-ho's love for his country and people, and I think it would be a good idea to stop by for a moment while passing by and meditate in silence to show respect and respect for the life of a person who sacrificed his life for the country.
